content: Where did the LORD send Jeremiah to receive His message?
explanation: God taught him with clay. “Go down at once to the potter’s house, and there I will reveal My message to you.” (Jeremiah 18:2, BSB)

content: At the potter's house, what did Jeremiah see the potter working at?
explanation: He was shaping clay. “So I went down to the potter’s house and saw him working at the wheel.” (Jeremiah 18:3, BSB)

content: At the potter's house, what was the potter shaping the vessel from?
explanation: God is like the potter. “But the vessel that he was shaping from the clay became flawed in his hand” (Jeremiah 18:4, BSB)

content: Jeremiah watched a potter. When the vessel became flawed, what did the potter do?
explanation: He reshaped it as seemed best. “so he formed it into another vessel, as it seemed best for him to do.” (Jeremiah 18:4, BSB)

content: After Jeremiah saw the potter, who did God say is like clay in His hand?
explanation: God can reshape His people. “Just like clay in the potter’s hand, so are you in My hand, O house of Israel.” (Jeremiah 18:6, BSB)

content: After the potter's house, what did God ask Israel through Jeremiah?
options: Can I not treat you as clay?
explanation: God has the right to reshape us. “can I not treat you as this potter treats his clay?” (Jeremiah 18:6, BSB)

content: Later, what did the LORD tell Jeremiah to buy from a potter?
explanation: It became another lesson for the elders. “Go and buy a clay jar from a potter.” (Jeremiah 19:1, BSB)

content: God told Jeremiah He knew him before when?
explanation: God set him apart as a prophet. “Before I formed you in the womb I knew you” (Jeremiah 1:5, BSB)

content: When God called Jeremiah, what excuse did he give?
explanation: God told him not to say that. “I surely do not know how to speak, for I am only a child!” (Jeremiah 1:6, BSB)

content: When God touched Jeremiah's mouth, what did He say He had put there?
explanation: Jeremiah would speak for God. “Behold, I have put My words in your mouth.” (Jeremiah 1:9, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, God says His plans for His people give them a future and what?
explanation: God's plans are good. “plans to prosper you and not to harm you, to give you a future and a hope.” (Jeremiah 29:11, BSB)

content: Why did God tell young Jeremiah not to be afraid?
explanation: God would deliver him. “Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you” (Jeremiah 1:8, BSB)

content: When God asked Jeremiah what he saw, what did he answer?
explanation: God watches over His word. “I see a branch of an almond tree” (Jeremiah 1:11, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, God says you will find Him when you search with all your what?
explanation: God is found by seekers. “You will seek Me and find Me when you search for Me with all your heart.” (Jeremiah 29:13, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, what does God promise to make with Israel and Judah?
explanation: His law will be on their hearts. “when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.” (Jeremiah 31:31, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah's new covenant, where will God write His law?
explanation: God's people will know Him. “I will put My law in their minds and inscribe it on their hearts.” (Jeremiah 31:33, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, what does God promise if you call to Him?
explanation: He shows great things. “Call to Me, and I will answer and show you great and unsearchable things you do not know.” (Jeremiah 33:3, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, the one who trusts the LORD is like what planted by the waters?
explanation: It does not fear heat or drought. “He is like a tree planted by the waters” (Jeremiah 17:8, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah's prayer, what is too difficult for God?
explanation: He made heaven and earth. “Nothing is too difficult for You!” (Jeremiah 32:17, BSB)

content: Who wrote down Jeremiah's words on a scroll?
explanation: Jeremiah dictated to him. “So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah” (Jeremiah 36:4, BSB)

content: As Jeremiah's scroll was read to him, what did King Jehoiakim do with it?
explanation: He cut it piece by piece. “Jehoiakim would cut them off with a scribe’s knife and throw them into the firepot” (Jeremiah 36:23, BSB)

content: What was at the bottom of the cistern Jeremiah was dropped into?
explanation: Jeremiah sank down in it. “which had no water but only mud, and Jeremiah sank down into the mud.” (Jeremiah 38:6, BSB)

content: Which court official rescued Jeremiah from the cistern?
explanation: He was a Cushite. “Now Ebed-melech the Cushite, a court official in the royal palace, heard that Jeremiah had been put into the cistern.” (Jeremiah 38:7, BSB)

content: To pull Jeremiah from the cistern, what did Ebed-melech tell him to put under his arms?
explanation: They padded the ropes. “Put these worn-out rags and clothes under your arms to pad the ropes.” (Jeremiah 38:12, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, how long would the nations serve the king of Babylon?
explanation: Daniel later read this prophecy. “and these nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.” (Jeremiah 25:11, BSB)

content: Jeremiah came from a family of priests in which town?
explanation: It was in Benjamin's territory. “one of the priests in Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin.” (Jeremiah 1:1, BSB)

content: Who was Jeremiah's father?
explanation: He was one of the priests. “These are the words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah” (Jeremiah 1:1, BSB)

content: Who read Jeremiah's scroll aloud to King Jehoiakim?
explanation: The king burned each section. “And as soon as Jehudi had read three or four columns” (Jeremiah 36:23, BSB)

content: How many men did the king send with Ebed-melech to rescue Jeremiah?
explanation: They pulled him out with ropes. “Take thirty men from here with you and pull Jeremiah the prophet out of the cistern before he dies.” (Jeremiah 38:10, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, which animal cannot change its spots?
explanation: Habitual evil is hard to change. “Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots?” (Jeremiah 13:23, BSB)

content: When Jeremiah tried not to speak God's message, what was it like in his heart?
explanation: He could not hold it in. “His message becomes a fire burning in my heart, shut up in my bones” (Jeremiah 20:9, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, which family refused to drink wine because of their forefather's command?
explanation: Jonadab son of Rechab commanded it. “for our forefather Jonadab son of Rechab commanded us” (Jeremiah 35:6, BSB)

content: In Jeremiah, what should a person boast about?
explanation: God delights in loving devotion. “But let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows Me” (Jeremiah 9:24, BSB)
